name: Sacramento International Airport
before:
Sacramento's main airport, ten and a half miles north west of downtown, and the largest public airport in California by land area at 6,000 acres. It is run by the Sacramento County Airport System, one of four airfields serving the city.

What makes it useful for an itinerary is what lies within reach. It is a practical gateway for Lake Tahoe and Heavenly, for Yosemite, for the Napa and Sonoma wine country and for the gold rush sites at Sutter's Mill and Marshall Gold Discovery State Historic Park, as well as the state capitol and Old Sacramento.

The airport has two parallel runways.
after:
Sacramento's main airport, about 10 miles north west of downtown on a site of roughly 6,000 acres. It is one of four airports run by the Sacramento County Department of Airports.

What makes it useful for an itinerary is what lies within reach: Lake Tahoe, Yosemite and the Napa and Sonoma wine country, as well as the State Capitol and Old Sacramento.

The airport has two parallel runways.

claims.note: Of the four county airports, the operator gives Sacramento International the passenger role (Mather cargo, Executive and Franklin Field general aviation). The FAA's CY2025 table lists no other Sacramento airport among commercial service airports.

claims.inAfter: about 10 miles north west of downtown
claims.note: Was 'ten and a half miles'. The written figures differ a little: Wikipedia 10.5 miles, the operator's 2020 Master Plan 'approximately 10 miles', the FAA master record 10 nautical miles (about 11.5 statute miles) and the operator's live history page '12 miles from downtown Sacramento'. The straight line from the GeoNames centre is 9.4 miles, and every one of these passes the coordinates check. The text uses the Master Plan's wording, which Wikipedia's 10.5 also supports; the 12 miles on the history page is not explained there.

claims.wasBefore: ten and a half miles north west of downtown
claims.why: Softened to the operator's own 'about 10 miles'; the written figures run from 10 to 12 miles (see the kept claim).

claims.claim: the largest public airport in California by land area
claims.wasBefore: and the largest public airport in California by land area at 6,000 acres
claims.why: Only Wikipedia ranks it, and Wikipedia's own sentence limits the ranking to commercial airports (military, cargo-only and general aviation fields excluded), so 'largest public airport' overstated it. The operator's pages, its Master Plan and the FAA record give the acreage but no ranking. The acreage is kept.

claims.claim: run by the Sacramento County Airport System, one of four airfields serving the city
claims.wasBefore: It is run by the Sacramento County Airport System, one of four airfields serving the city.
claims.why: Reworded with the operator's own name, the Sacramento County Department of Airports, which runs four airports (see the kept claim).

claims.claim: a practical gateway for Lake Tahoe and Heavenly
claims.wasBefore: It is a practical gateway for Lake Tahoe and Heavenly
claims.why: Heavenly rests on Wikipedia alone: the resort's own site (skiheavenly.com) answered a plain request with a bot-management block page ('The system cannot process your request', saved as zz-heavenly-plain) and was not read further, and Lake Tahoe's visitor authority does not mention the resort. 'Practical gateway' is softened to 'within reach' because the visitor authority calls Reno-Tahoe the closest airport and Sacramento about two hours' drive. Lake Tahoe itself is kept.

claims.claim: the gold rush sites at Sutter's Mill and Marshall Gold Discovery State Historic Park
claims.wasBefore: for the gold rush sites at Sutter's Mill and Marshall Gold Discovery State Historic Park
claims.why: Only Wikipedia ties the gold rush sites to the airport. California State Parks' page confirms the park at Coloma, on Highway 49 between Placerville and Auburn, but names no airport; El Dorado County's visitor site (visit-eldorado.com) answered both grab.mjs and grabb.mjs with a 'Checking the site connection security' page and was not tried again.

Held back: verified with two sources, but a new fact that replaces nothing in the old text, which gives no traffic figure. For Andy to add if he wants: 13,912,718 passengers in 2025, arriving plus departing (operator's December 2025 report; Wikipedia's infobox gives the same, citing the FAA), and 6,805,910 boardings in the FAA's preliminary CY2025 table (36th in the US). Southwest carried 3,770,548 of the 6,951,103 passengers the operator counts as enplaned, a little over half.
